newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called softer after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called softer after recent gains.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open flat to slightly lower Friday after this week's gains tied to steady cash market prices and strength in natural gas futures.
"They are softening a little. Quotes are actually pretty wide," said a West Coast electricity dealer.

In over-the-counter activity, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $14.20-14.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Thursday's settle at $14.35, while June Palo Verde (PV) at $19.50-19.90 versus yesterday's close at $19.60.
The NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas contract was down 3.3 cents at $2.210 per million British thermal units in early trading.
The dealer said the power complex would head lower today with weaker June gas futures which encountered technical resistance at $2.230.
Spot physical prices in the Northwest have been supported by cooler-than-normal spring weather, while those in the Southwest by hotter-than-normal temperatures, traders said.
Spot electricity supply across the West remained tight.

Hydropower availability in Northwest has been reduced due to flood control measures in effect in British Columbia and Bonneville Power Administration still limiting daily offers for peak demand hours.

About 4,000 megawatt (MW) of generating capacity in the Southwest is said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, but much of the capacity is expected to return to service later this month.
A 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was expected to return online today after being shut almost two weeks ago for repairs.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures would average near normal in the northeast to about two degrees F below normal southwest with chance of scattered precipitation this weekend, forecasters said.
In the Southwest, fair, dry weather is expected across the region with readings running near normal in the northeast to four degrees F above normal in the southwest.
Market sources said trading volume would be light due to many players absent to attend a golf tournament in Houston and an industry conference in Canada.
